content: The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT), a pivotal study focused on individuals with type 1 diabetes, provided clear evidence that maintaining intensive glycemic control, with an A1C level close to 7%, leads to a substantial reduction in the incidence of microvascular complications. These complications include diabetic retinopathy, neuropathy, and kidney disease, and the reduction rates range from 50% to 76% when compared to standard glycemic control, which corresponds to an A1C level of approximately 9%. Subsequent follow-up research conducted through the Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC) study has confirmed that the protective effects of intensive glycemic control on microvascular outcomes persist for decades. This is true even though the differences in glycemic control between the intensive and standard treatment groups have lessened over time.
